chapters.tldr: The first Incerto work: luck masquerading as skill, and skill as luck — the asymmetry that ruins both the lucky fool and the unlucky genius.
points: 'The tragedy is that much of what you think is random is in your control and, what's worse, the opposite.'
The hotshot: someone temporarily perceived to be important, rather than important to be temporary.
'The sucker's trap is when you focus on what you know and what others don't know, rather than the reverse.'
Never rid anyone of an illusion unless you can replace it in his mind with another illusion.

chapters.label: The Bed of Procrustes
chapters.tldr: Aphorisms on the Procrustean bed: we chop and stretch reality to fit neat categories, vocabularies, and narratives — and occasionally detonate things doing it.
points: 'The fool generalizes the particular; the nerd particularizes the general; the wise does neither.'
'You want to be yourself, idiosyncratic; the collective wants you generic to the point of castration.'
'To be permanently in a state of certainty is to be permanently dead.' — the bundle's whole critique in miniature.
Procrustes met Theseus and lay in his own bed — poetic justice as epistemology.

chapters.label: A Note on This Bundle
chapters.tldr: This epub's extractable text contains Antifragile's chapter summaries and glossary, Fooled by Randomness's aphorisms, and Bed of Procrustes in full — but The Black Swan appears only as a referenced title, not as text. Honest gap, declared rather than faked.
points: The Black Swan's core argument is summarized in this bundle's other three works — Mediocristan/Extremistan and the scandal of prediction.
Lindy in action: the Incerto has survived twenty years of hostile review — that survival is its own evidence.
Read the notes as a map; the full works reward the territory.

books.title: The Snowball
books.author: Alice Schroeder
books.tldr: The authorized biography with unprecedented access: Buffett's life as a case study in the inner scorecard — the obsessive collecting of money since age six, the trades and blunders, and the costs a snowball that big exacts on everyone in its path.
takeaways: The inner scorecard is the spine: would you rather be the world's best investor thought the worst, or the reverse? Buffett chose at nine.
Snowballs need wet snow and a long hill — time and reinvestment, not just rate of return.
The blunders are in the book by design: Dempster Mill, the textile mill he couldn't quit, Salomon's rot, Gen Re's derivative book.
Susie's leaving in 1977 broke the marriage contract he'd assumed was permanent — the biography's honest center.
The giving pledge logic: claim checks — money is claim checks on society's output; hoarding them past usefulness is failure.

chapters.label: Part 1 — The Bubble (Sun Valley 1999)
chapters.tldr: The frame: Buffett at the peak of the dot-com bubble, telling the world stocks can't grow to the sky — booed for it, right about it. The less flattering version, as he insisted biographers tell it.
points: He knew tech was outside his circle — 'risk comes from not knowing what you're doing.'
The Zegna jacket and the fifty-year-old office: the most ordinary-looking extraordinary man alive.
Schroeder's access condition: he would not review the manuscript.

chapters.label: Part 2 — The Inner Scorecard (Origins)
chapters.tldr: Omaha 1869 on: the Buffett grocery, Howard's failed depression-era politics, the paper routes and pinball machines — the childhood that built the machine.
points: Howard, 'a hundred percent Inner Scorecard guy' — the source of the whole philosophy.
Cherry Coke, racetrack odds, the arithmetic of everything — traits visible by age ten.
Dale Carnegie course certificate, January 1952: he invested in himself to conquer stage fright — the one diploma on the wall.

chapters.label: Part 3 — The Racetrack (Graham-Newman)
chapters.tldr: Columbia, Graham, the GEICO discovery-by-cab, then back to Omaha and the partnership: seven partnerships merged into one, compounding ~30% for thirteen years.
points: The Saturday GEICO visit as a nobody — pattern recognition plus the nerve to knock on doors.
Graham's rule: buy below working capital — and Buffett's amendment: buy wonderful businesses above it.
The windmill war and Dempster Mill: the activist chapter he preferred not to repeat.

chapters.label: Part 4 — Susie Sings (The Partnership Winds Down)
chapters.tldr: 1969: he closes the partnership at the top, distributes Berkshire, Diversified Retailing, and Blue Chip Stamps — the raw material of everything after. Susie's singing career begins; the marriage's fault line shows.
points: The dissolution letter: Berkshire worth ~$45/share, $16 of it textiles he wouldn't kill — 'I like the textile people.'
See's Candies' lesson lands in this era: pay up for franchises; never again buy cigar butts by reflex.
Susie: 'I don't want to be married to somebody who's going to spend his whole life sitting in front of a television eating hamburgers.' Both were right.

chapters.label: Part 5 — The King of Wall Street (Salomon)
chapters.tldr: The '87 crash he sailed through, the Coke stake ('a Mercedes for the price of a Chevrolet'), then Salomon Brothers 1991 — Mozer's false bids, and Buffett stepping in as chairman to save the firm.
points: Congress, TV cameras, and the line that saved Salomon: 'Lose money for the firm, and I will be understanding. Lose a shred of reputation for the firm, and I will be ruthless.'
He ran Salomon from Omaha by fax — proof the culture mattered more than the presence.
Flight 11 into the tower of his friend's world ended the era; 9/11 opened the last act.

chapters.label: Part 6 — Claim Checks (The Giving)
chapters.tldr: Susie's death in 2004, the 2006 pledge to give it all away via the Gates Foundation, and the Genie: 'You only get one mind and one body — it's got to last a lifetime.'
points: The car-genie speech to students: if it's the last car you'll ever get, you read the manual five times and fix every dent.
Claim checks: he came to see his fortune as society's spending vouchers, held in trust — hence giving it back rather than dynastying it.
The millennium New Year's Eve with the family: the snowball at rest, briefly, and what it rolled over to get there.
chapters.action: Take the scorecard test: one decision this week where you chose appearance over reality — re-run it inner-scorecard and note the difference.
